questions.text: In the text, what language term describes “old-fashioned”?
questions.passage: My oldest brother is quite different from me — he’s a bit old-fashioned really. I suppose he’s just very traditional. For example, he always wears a suit, a tie and leather shoes, listens to the radio and plays cricket. But the worst thing is that he’s got no sense of humour and that really gets on my nerves. I also get the impression that he thinks I’m pretty worthless, which doesn’t help our relationship. We rarely see each other these days. He sometimes calls in when he’s in the area and then we may go out together. But we usually end up arguing about which bus stop to walk to, or something silly like that.

I need to hear lots of spoken language to help me understand it, so sometimes I listen to people’s conversations in cafés.
I read over the notes of the key grammar points we covered in the last lesson before the next one.
I have quite a bit of free time and use it to study, so I like finding out how to use different resources, like grammar books.
I just want to learn practical things like ordering food in a restaurant.
I want to learn things like how to write essays and use a dictionary.
I’ve been told I’m a kinaesthetic learner, so I want a course to suit my learning style.
I studied English for several years at school, and now I just want to practise it informally and socially.
I want to use my English to talk about what’s going on in the world today.

After explaining second conditional rules, the teacher asks learners to find examples in an article and compare them with their first language.
The teacher gets learners to focus on collocations in a text about foreign travel and practise using them.
The teacher plays a recording of people complaining, drills complaint phrases, then learners prepare similar dialogues.
The teacher presents several ways of making requests. Learners practise them in pairs with prompt cards.
Learners think of words to complete “to have a(n) … on someone/one” and check their ideas in dictionaries.
I write on the topic for five minutes without worrying about mistakes. It helps me get ideas down on paper.
